themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 8 THIS WEEK compared to a 1.4-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 482% increase (z-score: 4.7)—suggesting a coordinated campaign or enforcement gap in Forest Hills/Rego Park.
evidence: 8 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (482% spike, z-score 4.7)
Statistically significant deviation with high-severity classification
No recent Reddit or news coverage suggests emerging, under-reported issue
reporting_angles: Ground-level canvassing: photograph and map illegal postings across key commercial corridors (Queens Boulevard, Yellowstone Boulevard) to identify patterns
Interview DSNY about enforcement frequency and whether staffing/budgets have changed this month

themes_detail.label: Panhandling Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints jumped to 7 LAST WEEK from a 0.6-complaint weekly baseline—a 1020% spike (z-score: 9.16, highest severity)—marking the sharpest rise in the 311 data and signaling an urgent street-level safety or economic crisis.
evidence: 7 panhandling complaints last week vs 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1020% increase, z-score 9.16—highest z-score in dataset)
Community board budget requests include 'Expand street outreach' (DHS) every year—unmet need
Aligns with 158% spike in 'Homeless Person Assistance' complaints 2 weeks ago (10 vs 3.9 avg)
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD Transit and precinct about whether panhandling has visibly increased on the streets and transit; identify specific hotspots (Forest Hills station, commercial zones)
Speak with local merchants and residents about safety perceptions; connect to DHS outreach capacity and whether street teams have been deployed to the area

themes_detail.label: Break-In / Property Crime Wave
themes_detail.summary: Door/window complaints surged to 11 LAST WEEK versus a 4.4-complaint weekly average—a 151% spike (z-score: 4.01)—suggesting either a localized break-in pattern or heightened resident anxiety about home security.
evidence: 11 door/window complaints last week vs 4.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (151% spike, z-score 4.01)
Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints average 412 over 90 days—possible related signal
No recent community board or news mentions, suggesting underreported neighborhood concern
reporting_angles: Obtain precinct-level crime data from NYPD: burglary, attempted burglary, and property crime trends for CD 406 over past 4 weeks to confirm spike
Interview residents who filed 311 complaints to understand timing and targets; speak with local police precinct about awareness and prevention messaging

themes_detail.label: Construction Activity Surge
themes_detail.summary: General construction/plumbing complaints jumped to 16 TWO WEEKS AGO from a 5.8-complaint weekly average—a 178% spike (z-score: 3.89)—coinciding with 4 active ULURP rezoning applications in the pipeline, suggesting either renovation pressures or uncoordinated work.
evidence: 16 construction/plumbing complaints 2 weeks ago vs 5.8 weekly average (178% increase, z-score 3.89)
297 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (242 alterations), suggesting sustained permit activity
4 active ULURP rezonings in early phases (Yellowstone Boulevard, 108-05 68th Road, 100-12 Queens Boulevard, 69-67 108th Street)
reporting_angles: Query DOB permit data: which addresses generated the spike 2 weeks ago? Are they tied to ULURP sites or independent renovations?
Interview community board about coordination between rezoning projects and resident complaints; check if there are violations or schedule violations

themes_detail.label: Animal Complaints & Unsanitary Conditions
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary animal private property complaints spiked to 3 LAST WEEK from a 0.4-complaint baseline—a 700% increase (z-score: 3.77)—suggesting either a pest infestation outbreak or poor enforcement of animal housing standards.
evidence: 3 unsanitary animal complaints last week vs 0.4 weekly average (700% increase, z-score 3.77)
No corresponding spike in general sanitation or pest-related complaints in top 10, suggesting issue is narrowly focused
Community board budget requests include environmental protection and park enhancement—possible neglected spaces
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD Animal Care & Control: have they received multiple calls to same address or area? Is this a boarding facility, illegal breeding, or hoarding situation?
Canvass neighborhoods for visual evidence of unsanitary conditions (e.g., overgrown lots, visible animals); connect to zoning and land-use enforcement
